# Save compatibility fixtures

The `season47-standings-legacy` save and `season47-standings-legacy-next` state were captured from unchanged `81fa080` before adding sourced standings rules. This public all-system career contains two leagues of five and four clubs, including byes. Every loaded source/test module was compared with that commit; the manifest records hashes and module count. Migration must retain the original ranking even though both leagues have French country metadata. `season47-continuation.test.js` verifies the independently captured next week. Never regenerate these expectations from new ranking code.

The `season46-calendar-legacy` save and `season46-calendar-legacy-next` state were captured from the original format-46 runtime at `2b2222a`, before calendar integration. Every loaded source/test module was compared against that commit before writing. The public synthetic career has variable 9/14/17/25-player squads and all management systems enabled. Its manifest retains gzip hashes and verified module count; `season46-continuation.test.js` checks exact independent continuation. Never regenerate these expectations from changed calendar code.

The gzip files contain UTF-8 JSON and use only Node's built-in `fs` and `zlib` in the migration test.

- `season19-pending-paid` is the genuine format19 pending transfer produced by `paid-midseason-scenarios.mjs` before the release-clause change (baseline `f0bf303`).
- `season19-pending-free-agent` is the genuine earlier free-agent scenario imported and saved by that baseline's format19 parser, before its schema20 edits.
- `season19-reply-*` retain the corresponding original next-matchday offers, new contracts, negotiation responses, transfers, ledger entries and wage agreements. They were extracted from the pre-change accepted scenarios, not generated by the code under test.

The migration tests compare complete imported states and independent recorded replies. These fixtures intentionally have no release clauses or transfer-mode fields.

- `season20-scouting-pending` and `season20-scouting-reply` were captured before named scout recruitment. They preserve an observation already queued under the original rules and its independently recorded reply, staff charges, knowledge and next match.
- `season21-training-scouts` and `season21-training-scouts-next` are complete format21 saves captured before fitness coaching changed the training engine. The seed227 Rhine career has a hired scout, named completed observation, pending assignment, a completed heavy-training week and an actual injury. The second file records the next week produced by the original engine. Migration compares both complete states, including injuries, training, scouting, staff, finances and the next prepared match; fitness remains disabled until explicitly enabled.
- `season22-injury-fitness-scouts`, `season22-injury-fitness-scouts-next` and `season22-injury-fitness-scouts-partial` are complete genuine format22 saves captured before physiotherapists or rehabilitation were added. The first imports the actual fitness-injury scenario at matchday two: the seed227 Rhine career has active fitness/scouting, a September 5 ankle injury diagnosed through September 25, and retained prior reports. The next two files were produced independently with the unchanged format22 world commands. They preserve a fully unavailable training week followed by a partially available week, including complete injury dates, training, finances, appointments and prepared matches.
- `season23-staff-rehabilitation-transfer` and `season23-staff-rehabilitation-transfer-next` are complete format23 saves captured before assistant-coach recruitment. The seed227 Rhine career has coaches, scouts, fitness coaches and physios, earned rehabilitation and a completed paid transfer of the injured player to Aegean. The first state is matchday three; the second was produced by the unchanged format23 world and also matched the independently retained transfer continuation. Full-state migration checks preserve the original diagnosis, the new club's treatment credits, all staff fees, installment debts, reports and next match.
- `season24-assistant-rehabilitation-transfer` and `season24-assistant-rehabilitation-transfer-next` are complete format24 saves captured before academy prospects or youth coaches were introduced. The seed227 Rhine career retains all five staff roles, including a prospectively hired assistant, a completed transfer of an injured player, scouting reports, training and rehabilitation. The untouched format24 world independently produced matchdays four and five; both files passed strict roundtrip validation before academy changes. They preserve the full senior catalog, payroll and installment history, five then eight treatment records, and the prepared matches.
- `season25-academy-career` and `season25-academy-career-next` preserve genuine format25 matchdays six and seven before senior aging or retirement. The seed227 Rhine career has all six staff roles, a trained academy graduate registered in the senior squad, youth and senior development, observations and normal payroll. `season25-academy-season-complete` and `season25-academy-next-season` independently preserve an actual season transition after a three-year graduate renewal, delegated recruitment and completion of the dated offseason window. All four complete files passed the unchanged format25 parser and serializer before lifecycle changes.
- `season25-academy-year4` is the genuine seed912 format25 academy age-out opening already generated during academy validation, before lifecycle work. It retains three seasons of actual contracts, matches and development. Lifecycle tests use this unchanged older career to submit a real three-year paid offer, then activate retirement before or after withdrawing that proposal; no version number or historical outcome was rewritten to create the fixture.
- `season26-retirement-year6` is the seed227 opening captured by the delegated lifecycle population diagnostic using actual world commands and the final retirement policy. It preserves six effective retirements, their previous registered squads, dated aging, development and every historical recruitment window. Tests strictly replay the complete save, continue its next matchday, and reject altered notices, source boundaries or practice evidence. Its compressed size is about142kB; larger twenty- and thirty-season diagnostics stay in ignored artifacts.
- `season26-lifecycle-career` and `season26-lifecycle-career-next` preserve genuine format26 matchdays seven and eight before youth competition was implemented. The seed227 Rhine career includes all six paid staff roles, a promoted academy graduate, age-weighted senior practice, academy weekly development and an immutable retirement notice. `season26-lifecycle-complete` and `season26-lifecycle-opening` independently retain the completed first offseason and the next season opening after an actual three-year graduate renewal and delegated recruitment. Every file passed the unchanged format26 parser and serializer; no historical youth fixtures or replacement prospects were added.

- `season27-youth-career` and `season27-youth-career-next` retain genuine format27 matchdays seven and eight captured before facilities were implemented. The seed227 Rhine career includes all six staff roles, senior rehabilitation, a promoted graduate, lifecycle aging, actual youth fixtures and an injury-reduced academy week. `season27-youth-complete` and `season27-youth-opening` independently retain the finished dated offseason and the next opening following a real three-year graduate renewal and delegated recruitment. All four files passed the unchanged format27 parser and serializer before runtime edits; the migration tests compare complete independent continuations with facilities disabled.

- `season28-facilities-career` and `season28-facilities-career-next` retain genuine format28 matchdays five and six captured before relationships or morale were implemented. The seed227 Rhine career has completed training facilities and actual practice gains, ongoing arena construction, all staff roles and a pending academy promotion accepted at the independent next boundary. `season28-facilities-complete` and `season28-facilities-opening` retain the actual dated offseason and next opening, including completed arena work, ongoing AI construction, upkeep, promotion, graduation and historical results. Every complete file passed the unchanged format28 parser/serializer before runtime edits.

The `season29-relationships-*` fixtures were generated by the unmodified schema-29 runtime before board implementation. The career file has an active playing-time promise at matchday five, its independent next file records matchday six, and the complete/opening pair records the actual offseason transition into year two. They retain enabled relationships, frozen morale, facilities and other existing systems; `capture-board-baseline.mjs` and `board-baseline-report.json` under `.artifacts` record generation.

The `season30-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-30 saves captured with the committed `scripts/capture-season-fixtures.mjs` at `f1a8449`, whose runtime is unchanged from the handover commit `acc5c27`, before sponsorship negotiations or any format-31 work. The script creates the seed227 Rhine career exactly like the New career screen (standard injuries, every new-career system and a manager profile), sets a manual EUR 22 ticket price, starts a training-facility upgrade after matchday one and otherwise uses ordinary world commands with automatic substitutions. `career` is matchday five with four board reviews; `career-next` is the independently produced matchday six; `complete` finishes the season and the dated offseason under delegated contracts; `opening` is the resulting season-two opening. `tests/season30-continuation.test.js` checks the continuations and round trips. The script refuses to overwrite existing fixtures unless `--force` is passed; regenerate only on unchanged format-30 code.

The `season31-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-31 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` at `a947425`, after sponsorship negotiations and before Level 7 step 7.2 (board funding requests). The same seed227 Rhine career setup as the format-30 set now has negotiations enabled: `career` is matchday five before any offer, `career-next` is matchday six with three open offers for the manually controlled club while rival clubs have signed automatically, `complete` finishes the season and offseason without the manager signing, and `opening` is the season-two opening in which those offers expired and the club has no main sponsor. `tests/season31-continuation.test.js` checks the continuations and round trips.

The `season32-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-32 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` at `ecf460c`, after board funding requests (Level 7 step 7.2) and before step 7.3 (board consequences). The same seed227 Rhine career setup now also has board funding requests enabled: `career` is matchday five and `career-next` matchday six, neither with a funding decision yet; `complete` is the finished first season after the offseason market, including Aegean Waves' automatic approved request with its `board-capital` ledger entry and funded upgrade; `opening` is the rolled-over second season. `tests/season32-continuation.test.js` checks that the current runtime continues each file exactly as recorded.

The `season33-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-33 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` at `a93f82f`, after board season verdicts (Level 7 step 7.3) and before step 7.4 (press and player events). The same seed227 Rhine career setup now also has season verdicts enabled from the career's start: `career` and `career-next` are matchdays five and six, `complete` is the finished first season after the offseason market with every club's final review, and `opening` is the second season, whose staff budgets and owner capital follow those verdicts (Aegean Waves Confident, Adriatic Comets Under pressure). `tests/season33-continuation.test.js` checks that the current runtime continues each file exactly as recorded.

The `season34-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-34 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` after press conferences and the Inbox (Level 7 step 7.4) and before step 7.6 (rivalries). From this capture the script also answers an open press question with the first offered answer: the seed227 Rhine career reaches matchday five after three wins, so every file carries the recorded "Credit the whole squad" answer, and `career-next` freezes its morale effect for matchday six. `complete` and `opening` are the finished first season and the second-season opening. `tests/season34-continuation.test.js` checks that the current runtime continues each file exactly as recorded.

The `season35-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-35 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` after rivalries (Level 7 step 7.6) and before step 7.7 (facility maintenance). The seed227 Rhine career now has rivalries from the opening matchday, so board reviews record derby contributions (Rhine Falcons' river-derby win adds 3), alongside the recorded press answer and many completed facility upgrades across the league. `tests/season35-continuation.test.js` checks that the current runtime continues each file exactly as recorded.

The `season36-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-36 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` after facility upkeep plans (Level 7 step 7.7) and before step 7.5 (dismissal and job changes). Upkeep choices are enabled from the opening day; no club reduced its upkeep in this career, so the files record the anchor without upkeep events, alongside rivalries, derby reviews and the recorded press answer. `tests/season36-continuation.test.js` checks that the current runtime continues each file exactly as recorded.

The `season37-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-37 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` after the club-change groundwork (Level 7 step 7.5a) and before dismissal and job offers (step 7.5b). New careers record the career switch from the opening day with no moves. Migrating them to format 38 judges only season ends still to come, so the completed and next-season files start decisions with season 2. `tests/season37-continuation.test.js` checks that the current runtime continues each file exactly as recorded.

The `season38-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-38 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` from the committed Level 7 / pilot 2.7 code (the work in progress was set aside with `git stash`) before format 39 let careers carry their own world (real-data pilot step 2.8a). They are careers in the built-in league and store no world; `tests/season38-continuation.test.js` checks that they load, continue and roll over exactly as recorded. Replaying the same career with the format-39 code gave identical contents.

The `season39-board-*` fixtures are genuine format-39 saves captured with `npm run fixtures:capture` from the working tree after step 2.8c and before format 40 introduced the compact save layout (step 2.8d). The `season39-world8-*` fixtures are format-39 saves of an eight-club test world (`tests/world-fixtures.ts`, renamed built-in clubs, no real data) after six and seven matchdays, captured by a one-off test at the same point. `tests/season39-continuation.test.js` checks that both kinds continue, roll over and round-trip through the current plain and compact layouts.

The four `season44-*` fixtures listed in `senior-history-original-44.json` were captured from untouched commit `7f76294` before format 45 and senior summaries were implemented. The manifest records the source fixture hashes, source commit and captured gzip hashes. They include the ordinary board career, complete season, next opening and an eight-club career opening. `senior-history.test.js` checks original all-player totals, historical manager logs, relationship reports, migration, corruption rejection and idempotence. Do not regenerate these baselines with the summarized runtime.

The `season48-postseason-legacy*` files (manifest with SHA-256 hashes) are a genuine format-48 public 5+4-club domestic career and its next week, captured with `.artifacts/capture-postseason-baseline.mjs` from untouched commit `7db0d89` (115 modules verified) before format 49 added postseasons; `tests/season48-continuation.test.js` checks it keeps its regular-season-only calendar and continues exactly. The `season49-divisions-legacy*` files are a genuine format-49 public two-division career at the opening of season two and its next week, captured with `.artifacts/capture-divisions-baseline.mjs` from the uncommitted 3.4a-3.4b working tree before format 50 (116 loaded modules hashed in the manifest); `tests/division-changes.test.js` checks the upgrade keeps the divisions already played and continues exactly. Never regenerate either from later code.

The `season50-tiebreak-legacy-*` files are genuine format-50 saves (compact envelopes) of a public two-division career (`format-baseline-test`, seed 5150, the test world of `tests/division-changes.test.js`), captured with the committed `scripts/capture-format-baseline.mjs tiebreak-legacy` from unchanged commit `e0679b8` before format 51 added the FIBA default standings rule. `mid` is season one after three weeks and `mid-next` its next week; `complete` is season one finished with the market closed and `opening` its rollover into season two. The manifest records each file's SHA-256 and the 116 loaded source modules. `tests/season50-continuation.test.js` checks that the career keeps its prototype ranking and its recorded divisions and continues exactly. The script is reusable: run it with a new label on unchanged code before the next format change. Never regenerate these files from later code.

Never regenerate them from later code.
